dedupe_keys.name: physical and socio economic characteristics of global large inland waterways

description: This dataset gives the physical and socio-economic characteristics of inland waterways on 66 large rivers whose basins exceed 100,000 km2, for 2015. It holds two shapefiles: one at reach scale with freeze-up duration, actual and idealised minimum maintenance depth and actual and idealised bearing capacity (navigable freight capacity in 100 million tonnes per year), and one at basin scale with bearing capacity, GDP, population, agriculture and industry output and the human development index. It was produced by Yichu Wang, Xiabin Chen, Alistair Borthwick, Tianhong Li, Huaihan Liu, Shengfa Yang, Chunmiao Zheng and Jianhua Xu. Coverage is global for the 66 large rivers, in WGS 84. Access: free download from figshare under CC BY 4.0 as a 15 MB RAR archive (version 1, March 2020). Caveats: it is a single-year snapshot, capacities are estimates, and the archive format needs a RAR tool. It supports global comparisons of inland waterway capacity, screening of drought and low-water exposure of navigation and long-term freight capacity planning, and complements the US national waterway network and the Polish inland waterways portal catalogued here.
